version.changelog: mcp --transport https: serve MCP over HTTPS with bearer tokens (HLD §16)

llm.summary: The skill is a disclosed, read-only VMware log search integration, with credential and audit-log handling that users should configure carefully.

dimensions.detail: The skill needs appliance host, username, password environment variables, and network access to the configured Log Insight appliance, which is expected for this purpose; users should use a read-only service account.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses a pinned uv/PyPI package and Bash CLI commands; this is coherent for an MCP/CLI integration, though the package code itself is not bundled in the inspected artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions are scoped to VMware log investigation, include routing boundaries for related VMware skills, and explicitly warn that log text is untrusted data rather than agent instructions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill documents local config under ~/.vmware-log-insight, password loading from a chmod 600 .env file, automatic b64 obfuscation of plaintext .env passwords, and per-call audit records in ~/.vmware/audit.db; these are disclosed and purpose-aligned but retain sensitive operational metadata locally.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is querying VMware Log Insight / Aria Operations for Logs, and the documented tool surface is limited to seven read-only operations for logs, fields, versions, alerts, and alert history.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intend to let the agent read VMware Log Insight data. Configure a least-privilege read-only service account, prefer injecting the password from a secret manager rather than storing it in .env, keep local config and audit files protected, and leave TLS verification enabled except for controlled lab appliances.
llm.findings:
[TM1] expected: The --skip-auth flag applies to the diagnostic doctor command, not to log-query defaults or MCP operation, so the artifact does not support tool-parameter abuse.
[TM3] expected: The same --skip-auth reference is a diagnostic option; authentication remains part of normal configuration and TLS verification is documented as enabled by default.
[PE3] expected: The .env password handling is real credential-at-rest exposure, but it is disclosed, tied to authenticating to the target appliance, recommends chmod 600, and advises secret-manager injection for stronger secrecy.
[RA2] expected: Local config files and the shared audit database are disclosed persistence for configuration and auditing, not hidden backdoor persistence or autonomous background execution.
[PE2] expected: The chmod 600 command restricts file permissions and does not invoke sudo or root execution.
